title: Neutral tensor reconstruction, generators and tangent families
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small $k$-linear abelian category [def-sp-abelian], meaning that its isomorphism classes form a set in the object universe and each morphism set is a $k$-vector space with bilinear composition. Equip it with a $k$-bilinear monoidal product [def-sfb-monoidal-category], symmetry isomorphisms satisfying the symmetric monoidal identities, and a unit $\mathbf1$ with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$. Assume every object has a dual, with evaluation and coevaluation satisfying the two triangle identities. Let $\omega$ be a faithful exact $k$-linear symmetric tensor functor to finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces: it injects every morphism set, preserves short exact sequences, and identifies products, unit, symmetry, evaluation and coevaluation with their usual vector-space counterparts. Fix a small skeleton to index families.

For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, let $H(A)$ consist of families of invertible $A$-linear maps $a_V$ on $A\otimes_k\omega(V)$, natural for all morphisms in $\mathcal C$, with $a_{V\otimes W}=a_V\otimes a_W$ and $a_{\mathbf1}=1$. Then $H$ is represented by an affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Its tautological actions give an equivalence $\mathcal C\simeq\operatorname{Rep}_k(H)$ preserving underlying vector spaces and tensor products; a rational representation means a homomorphism to $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ [def-wf-algebraic-representations], with $\operatorname{GL}(V)(A)=\operatorname{Aut}_A(A\otimes_kV)$. If an object $W$ tensor-generates $\mathcal C$, meaning every object is a subquotient of a finite direct sum of tensor words in $W,W^\vee$, then $H\to\operatorname{GL}(\omega(W))$ is a closed immersion, and $H$ is of finite type over $k$. A subquotient means a quotient of a subobject.

The tangent Lie algebra $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\ker(H(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2)\to H(k))$ identifies with natural families $D_V\in\operatorname{End}_k(\omega(V))$ satisfying $D_{V\otimes W}=D_V\otimes1+1\otimes D_W$ and $D_{\mathbf1}=0$, with componentwise commutator bracket. Under this identification the differential of the tautological action on $\omega(V)$ is $D\mapsto D_V$. The standard vector-space operations on this kernel are the tangent operations [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space, def-sc-dual-numbers]. For any affine group scheme $K$ of finite type, differentials of rational representations define a tensor functor from $\operatorname{Rep}_k(K)$ to the finite-dimensional representations of $\operatorname{Lie}(K)$ [def-wf-lie-algebra], and $d\operatorname{Ad}(x)(y)=[x,y]$. All spaces lie in a fixed universe and the families in a containing universe.

source.place: Theorems 9.24 and 9.46--9.47, Notes 9.25--9.27, printed pp.172--173,182--184; Lie tangent-family description is the dual-number calculation in Lemma 23.69, p.506. Differentiation and adjoint bracket: Theorem 10.23, pp.193--194; tensor differential: 10.28, pp.194--195. No existence of a semisimple group is asserted here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-exact-fibre-coalgebra-reconstruction] to the underlying abelian category and $\omega$. Its hypotheses are precisely essential smallness and faithful exact linearity, all assumed here. Write $c_V(\phi,v)=[\phi\otimes v]_V$ for its coefficient classes. They span the resulting coalgebra $B$, satisfy $c_W(\psi,\omega(f)v)=c_V(\psi\omega(f),v)$, and give the stated equivalence with finite-dimensional right $B$-comodules. Work with the fixed skeleton, transporting tensor objects and duals along their chosen representative isomorphisms; the displayed naturality relation makes this transport independent of those isomorphisms.

Define multiplication and unit on this actual coefficient quotient by
$$c_V(\phi,v)c_W(\psi,w)=c_{V\otimes W}(\phi\otimes\psi,v\otimes w),\qquad 1_B=c_{\mathbf1}(1,1).$$
The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extends this formula bilinearly. A relation for $f:V\to V'$ multiplied by a coefficient of $W$ becomes the relation for $f\otimes1_W$; the relation in the other factor becomes that for $1_V\otimes g$. Thus it descends to $B$. Associativity follows by applying the relation to the associator; the two unit identities follow by applying it to the unitors. Applying it to the symmetry gives commutativity. These maps have their usual underlying-vector-space formulas by the hypothesis on $\omega$. For tensor-product bases, the formula for $\Delta$ in Step 1 gives $\Delta(cc')=\Delta(c)\Delta(c')$; evaluation gives $\epsilon(cc')=\epsilon(c)\epsilon(c')$, and the one-dimensional unit gives $\Delta(1)=1\otimes1$, $\epsilon(1)=1$. Each equality holds on the spanning coefficient classes and hence everywhere. We have constructed a commutative bialgebra, without invoking a tensor reconstruction theorem.

source.place: 9.44-9.45, pp.181-182; coefficient verification of their bialgebra construction

proof.text:
For $v\in\omega(V)$ let $\widehat v$ be evaluation at $v$ on $\omega(V)^*$. Define
$$S(c_V(\phi,v))=c_{V^\vee}(\widehat v,\phi).$$
This is well-defined: the dual morphism of $f$ acts by precomposition with $\omega(f)$, and the relation for $f^\vee$ is exactly the image of the relation for $f$. The identification $(V\otimes W)^\vee\simeq W^\vee\otimes V^\vee$ and the symmetry show $S(cc')=S(c)S(c')$ and $S(1)=1$. Put $C_{ij}=c_V(e_i^*,e_j)$ and $Q_{ij}=c_{V^\vee}(\widehat e_i,e_j^*)=S(C_{ji})$. Naturality for evaluation and coevaluation gives respectively $Q^{\mathsf t}C=I$ and $CQ^{\mathsf t}=I$: their $(i,j)$ entries are the coefficients of evaluation on $e_i^*\otimes e_j$, and coevaluation $1\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes e_i^*$. Thus $\sum_a S(C_{ia})C_{aj}=\delta_{ij}=\sum_a C_{ia}S(C_{aj})$. These are both antipode identities on all matrix coefficients, which span $B$. Therefore $B$ is a commutative Hopf algebra. Both triangle identities, and both orders of inverse, have been used.

source.place: 9.46-9.47, pp.182-184; rigidity supplies inverses by evaluation and coevaluation

proof.text: Let $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with the group structure supplied by [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor]. A linear map $t:B\to A$ is equivalent to a natural family $a_V$ of $A$-linear endomorphisms: in a finite basis set $a_V(1\otimes v)=\sum_i t(c_V(e_i^*,v))\otimes e_i$; conversely set $t(c_V(\phi,v))=(1\otimes\phi)a_V(1\otimes v)$. Bilinearity and the quotient relations prove that these formulas are well-defined and inverse. By the product and unit formulas in Step 2, $t$ is a unital algebra map exactly when $a$ respects tensors and the unit. Step 3 gives an inverse family by composing $t$ with $S$. The comultiplication formula gives $(t*u)(C_{ij})=\sum_a t(C_{ia})u(C_{aj})$, so the group law is composition of families. [def-weil-affine-spectrum] now identifies $G(A)$ with exactly $H(A)$, naturally for every algebra $A$, including nonreduced and zero algebras. Hence $G$ represents $H$.

For this possibly infinite-type affine group the comodule/action identification can be checked directly. Given $\rho(v)=\sum_i v_i\otimes b_i$, let a point $t:B\to A$ act by $1\otimes v\mapsto\sum_i t(b_i)\otimes v_i$. Coassociativity, counit and antipode give multiplication, identity and inverse. This is a group-scheme representation on a finite-dimensional space because its coefficient matrix has the inverse supplied by the antipode: hence its determinant is a unit and the coefficients define an algebra map from the coordinate ring in [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Apply [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; for the zero space the action is the unique trivial action. Conversely evaluate a representation on the universal point $\mathrm{id}_B\in G(B)$ to obtain $\rho$. Multiplication and identity evaluated on the universal pair over $B\otimes B$ give the two comodule identities. The constructions are inverse by naturality under $t:B\to A$. A linear map is equivariant exactly when it commutes with the universal coactions, by evaluating at $\mathrm{id}_B$. The tensor coaction is $v\otimes w\mapsto\sum(v_i\otimes w_j)\otimes b_i b'_j$; the unit coaction is $1\mapsto1\otimes1$. Thus Step 1's equivalence is the tautological equivalence with $\operatorname{Rep}_k(H)$ and preserves the specified underlying vector spaces and tensors. No finite-type version of the representation dictionary is used for $H$.

source.place: 9.46, pp.182-183, Comod(C) to Rep(G); pointwise formulas of 4.1, p.84

proof.text: Suppose $W$ tensor-generates and choose a basis of $\omega(W)$, of dimension $n$. Let $C=(C_{ij})$ be its coefficient matrix. Step 3 makes $S(C)$ its inverse; coefficients of $W^\vee$ are the transposed inverse entries. Let $B_0$ be the subalgebra generated by entries of $C$ and $C^{-1}$. Tensor coefficients are products and direct-sum coefficients are linear combinations. Coefficients of subobjects introduce nothing new: for $i:U\hookrightarrow T$, extend a functional $\phi$ on $\omega(U)$ to a functional $\widetilde\phi$ on $\omega(T)$ using a finite basis, so $c_U(\phi,u)=c_T(\widetilde\phi,\omega(i)u)$. For a quotient $q:U\twoheadrightarrow V$, lift $v$ to $u$ using exactness of $\omega$; then $c_V(\psi,v)=c_U(\psi\omega(q),u)$. Consequently every coefficient lies in $B_0$ and $B=B_0$. If $n>0$, determinant multiplicativity [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] gives $\det C\det C^{-1}=1$; [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] gives $C^{-1}=(\det C)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(C)$. Therefore $B$ is generated by the $n^2$ entries of $C$ and $(\det C)^{-1}$.

source.place: 9.27, p.173, tensor generation; matrix-coefficient proof of the closed immersion

proof.text: For $n>0$, the representation of $W$ is dual to the map $k[x_{ij},(\det x)^{-1}]\to B$ sending $x_{ij}$ to $C_{ij}$, by [def-sc-general-linear-group] and the action formula of Step 5. Step 6 proves surjectivity. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] to the single affine open equal to the whole target: the source is $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and its map on global sections is that surjection. Thus $H\to\operatorname{GL}(\omega(W))$ is a closed immersion. Also $B$ is finitely generated over $k$, so its spectrum has the single finite-type affine chart over $\operatorname{Spec}k$; this is the finite-affine-cover criterion in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $n=0$, faithfulness implies $W=0$. Every tensor word is zero unless it is the empty word $\mathbf1$, so Step 6 instead gives $B=k$; then $H$ and $\operatorname{GL}(0)$ are the trivial group $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the assertion still holds.

source.place: 9.27, p.173; Stacks Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion, affine criterion; finite-type definition

proof.text: Put $E=k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$ [def-sc-dual-numbers]. A component of a family in the kernel of $H(E)\to H(k)$ has a unique expression $1+\varepsilon D_V$ in a finite basis, with inverse $1-\varepsilon D_V$. Comparing coefficients of $\varepsilon$ in naturality gives $D_W\omega(f)=\omega(f)D_V$; comparison in the tensor identity gives $D_{V\otimes W}=D_V\otimes1+1\otimes D_W$, and in the unit gives $D_{\mathbf1}=0$. Conversely these equations give a kernel family. Addition from [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] uses the algebra with basis $1,\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2$ and all products of the $\varepsilon_i$ zero: its component is $1+\varepsilon_1D_V+\varepsilon_2E_V$, whose pullback $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\mapsto\varepsilon$ has coefficient $D_V+E_V$. Scaling $\varepsilon\mapsto a\varepsilon$ gives $aD_V$. Thus the bijection is linear for precisely the stipulated tangent operations, without finite type of $H$.

Write a point in Step 8 as $\epsilon+\varepsilon d:B\to E$. Being multiplicative is exactly $d(bb')=\epsilon(b)d(b')+d(b)\epsilon(b')$, by multiplying its constant and $\varepsilon$ parts. The tangent Lie bracket is the convolution commutator $[d,e]=d*e-e*d$ by [lem-sfb-bialgebra-distribution-tangent-calculus], which applies to the commutative bialgebra of Step 2 without any finiteness assumption. On a coefficient, $d(c_V(\phi,v))=\phi(D_Vv)$; hence
$$(d*e)(c_V(\phi,v))=\sum_i\phi(D_Ve_i)e_i^*(E_Vv)=\phi(D_VE_Vv).$$
Subtracting the reversed expression proves that the bracket is the componentwise commutator. In particular it again satisfies the family equations. The tautological action at $V$ sends $1+\varepsilon D$ to $1+\varepsilon D_V$, so its differential is exactly $D\mapsto D_V$. This computation also identifies the standard affine-group tangent bracket, defined by invariant derivations as in the cited node, rather than introducing a bracket with an unrelated convention.

Now let $K$ be any affine finite-type $k$-group scheme, with no smoothness or characteristic assumption. [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] says the differential of every rational representation $r:K\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ is a linear Lie homomorphism and $r(t_x)=1+\varepsilon dr(x)$. If $f:V\to U$ intertwines two representations, apply the intertwining equation to $t_x$ and compare $\varepsilon$ coefficients to obtain $f\,dr_V(x)=dr_U(x)f$. Thus the same linear maps define the functor on morphisms; identity and composition are preserved because their underlying linear maps are unchanged. For tensor representations,
$$(1+\varepsilon dr_V(x))\otimes(1+\varepsilon dr_U(x))=1+\varepsilon(dr_V(x)\otimes1+1\otimes dr_U(x)).$$
The unit representation differentiates to zero. The usual associativity, unit and symmetry linear maps remain intertwiners by the preceding morphism calculation, so this is a tensor functor to finite-dimensional Lie representations [def-wf-lie-algebra]. This tensor formula is calculated here; Proposition 10.28 is the derivation description, not itself a tensor-differentiation theorem.

source.place: 10.23, p.193; direct dual-number tensor computation after 10.18, p.191

proof.text:
The adjoint homomorphism for $K$ and its conjugation characterization on all algebra points are supplied by [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus]. Choose a closed immersion $\rho:K\to\operatorname{GL}_m$ from [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation]. Its differential is injective by the closed-subgroup clause of the dual-number node. Put $X=d\rho(x)$ and $Y=d\rho(y)$. Apply its adjoint-naturality formula with the algebra $k[s]/(s^2)$ and the point $t_x=1+sX$. Conjugating the scalar-extended tangent matrix $Y$ gives
$$(1+sX)Y(1-sX)=Y+s(XY-YX).$$
The constant term is the identity action and its $s$ coefficient is the differential of $\operatorname{Ad}$ applied to $y$. Thus $d\rho(d\operatorname{Ad}(x)(y))=XY-YX=d\rho([x,y])$, where the last equality is bracket preservation in [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus]. Injectivity gives $d\operatorname{Ad}(x)(y)=[x,y]$. This includes nonreduced finite-type groups.

proof_origin.place: Explicit coefficient-quotient realization of 9.37 and 9.44-9.47; coefficient argument for 9.27; dual-number calculation of 23.69 and 10.20-10.29. The tensor-differential formula is written out rather than misattributed to 10.28.
